```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# ── Inputs ──
# Parameter registry: the single source of every model value (see parameters/README.md).
reg_path <- normalizePath(params$registry, mustWork = TRUE)

# Patient-level BANDING-SET data. The database is not distributed with this repository
# (it is held by the study group). Give its path in params$data or in the environment
# variable BANDING_SET_DATA to re-estimate the empirical parameters and the descriptive
# sections. Without it, the report takes the empirical parameters (events / total) from
# the registry, which holds the same values, and skips the sections that need the raw data.
data_path <- if (nzchar(params$data)) params$data else Sys.getenv("BANDING_SET_DATA", unset = "")
have_data <- nzchar(data_path) && file.exists(data_path)

# Auto-detect version from filename (e.g. "Study_v1.0.Rmd" → "V1.0")
analysis_version <- {
  fn  <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(knitr::current_input()))
  hit <- regmatches(fn, regexpr("v[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+", fn, ignore.case = TRUE))
  if (length(hit) == 1) toupper(hit) else "V1.0"
}

# Figures (PNG 300 dpi and TIFF 600 dpi) are written next to the knitted HTML
pub_fig_dir <- "figures"
if (!dir.exists(pub_fig_dir)) dir.create(pub_fig_dir, recursive = TRUE)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = file.path(pub_fig_dir, "fig_"))

set.seed(2026)
```

```{r helpers, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ── Formatters ──
fmt_p <- function(p, digits = 3) {
  sapply(p, function(x) {
    if (is.na(x)) return("NA")
    if (x < 0.0005) return("<0.001")
    sprintf("%.3f", x)
  })
}

round_std <- function(x, digits = 0) {
  posneg <- sign(x)
  z      <- floor(abs(x) * 10^digits + 0.5) / 10^digits
  z * posneg
}

med_iqr <- function(x, digits = 1) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) return("—")
  fmt <- paste0("%.", digits, "f")
  sprintf(paste0(fmt, " (", fmt, "–", fmt, ")"),
          round_std(median(x), digits),
          round_std(quantile(x, 0.25, type = 2), digits),
          round_std(quantile(x, 0.75, type = 2), digits))
}

# Number with thousands separator and two decimals (format 1,000.00)
fmt_n <- function(x, d = 2) { x <- as.numeric(x); x[!is.na(x) & abs(x) < 0.5 * 10^(-d)] <- 0; formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",") }   # no "-0.00"
# Axis labels for amounts in euros: thousands separator and two decimals
eur_lab <- scales::label_comma(accuracy = 0.01)

# ── Statistical helpers ──
sw_test <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) < 3)    return(list(W = NA, p = NA, normal = NA))
  if (length(x) > 5000) x <- sample(x, 5000)
  t <- shapiro.test(x)
  list(W = round(t$statistic, 3), p = round(t$p.value, 4),
       normal = t$p.value >= 0.05)
}

cat_test <- function(x, g) {
  tbl <- table(x, g)
  if (any(dim(tbl) < 2)) return(list(p = NA, method = "NA"))
  exp_cells <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tbl, simulate.p.value = FALSE)$expected)
  if (any(exp_cells < 5)) {
    t <- fisher.test(tbl, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 10000)
    return(list(p = t$p.value, method = "Fisher's exact"))
  }
  t <- chisq.test(tbl)
  list(p = t$p.value, method = "Chi-square")
}

wilson_ci <- function(x, n, conf = 0.95) {
  if (is.na(n) || n <= 0) return(c(NA, NA))
  z   <- qnorm(1 - (1 - conf) / 2)
  p   <- x / n
  den <- 1 + z^2 / n
  cen <- (p + z^2 / (2 * n)) / den
  half <- (z * sqrt((p * (1 - p) / n) + (z^2 / (4 * n^2)))) / den
  c(max(0, cen - half), min(1, cen + half))
}
```

```{r load-data}
if (have_data) {
raw <- readxl::read_excel(data_path, sheet = "ARREGLAT", skip = 1, .name_repair = "minimal")

# The sheet has a grouping row above the header (hence skip = 1) and
# unnamed separator columns, which are dropped.
raw <- raw[, names(raw) != "" & !duplicated(names(raw))]
num <- function(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gsub(",", ".", as.character(x))))

benignas <- c("Leiomioma", "Pàncrees ectòpic", "Lipoma", "Pòlip fibroide", "Brunner",
              "Hiperplàsia foveolar (Ménétrier)", "Ectòpia gàstrica")
col_1a <- "Èxit clínic a 1 any (=desparició lesió?)"

dat <- raw |>
  transmute(
    id          = row_number(),
    edad        = num(edad),
    sexo        = factor(ifelse(as.character(sexo) == "2", "Female",
                         ifelse(as.character(sexo) == "1", "Male", NA)), levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    tam_mm      = num(ecoend_lesion_tamano),
    loc         = factor(c("1" = "Oesophagus", "2" = "Stomach", "3" = "Duodenum", "4" = "Rectum")[as.character(num(ecoend_lesion_localizacion))],
                         levels = c("Oesophagus", "Stomach", "Duodenum", "Rectum")),
    capa        = factor(c("1" = "Superficial", "2" = "Deep")[as.character(num(ecoend_lesion_capas))],
                         levels = c("Superficial", "Deep")),
    incidental  = as.character(hallazgo_casual),
    dx_def      = as.character(biopsia_diagnostico_def),
    histo       = case_when(dx_def %in% benignas ~ "Benign",
                            dx_def == "GIST" ~ "GIST",
                            dx_def %in% c("TNE", "Biòpsia prèvia: TNE") ~ "NET",
                            TRUE ~ "Unknown"),
    bx_previa   = dx_def == "Biòpsia prèvia: TNE",
    tec_ok      = as.character(lbsr_exito_tecnico) == "1",
    bx_estado   = as.character(biopsia_si_no_diagnostico),
    res_1a      = as.character(.data[[col_1a]]),
    ea          = as.character(ea_si_no) == "2",
    sed_anest   = as.character(sedacion_anestesista) == "1"
  ) |>
  mutate(histo = factor(histo, levels = c("Benign", "GIST", "NET", "Unknown")))

# ── Analysis population (editor comment 1): SET ≤10 mm, oesophagus or
#    stomach (ESGE 2022 only supports surveillance at these locations) and
#    incidental finding.
flow <- list(total = nrow(dat))
d1 <- dat |> filter(!is.na(tam_mm) & tam_mm <= 10);           flow$le10 <- nrow(d1)
d2 <- d1  |> filter(loc %in% c("Oesophagus", "Stomach"));        flow$eg   <- nrow(d2)
an <- d2  |> filter(incidental == "1");                        flow$an   <- nrow(an)
flow$gt10   <- flow$total - flow$le10
flow$other  <- flow$le10 - flow$eg
flow$noinc  <- flow$eg - flow$an
} else {
  # Without the raw data: lesions in the published cohort (Bas-Cutrina 2023) and in the
  # analysed subgroup (incidental oesophageal or gastric SET <= 10 mm); the budget impact
  # uses their ratio. The flow diagram and the descriptive sections are skipped.
  an   <- NULL
  flow <- list(total = 122L, an = 60L)
}
```

# Purpose of this report

This report is the analysis behind the manuscript *Endoscopic Band Ligation + SINK Biopsy vs ESGE Surveillance for Small Oesophagogastric Subepithelial Tumours: A Cost-Consequence Analysis* (Revista Española de Enfermedades Digestivas, reference 12126/2026). The model was built from scratch for the resubmission and answers point by point the methodological comments of the editor (section 3).

- **Question:** for an incidentally detected oesophageal or gastric SET of 10 mm or less, is surveillance according to the European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE 2022) or upfront EUS plus EBL-SINK preferable?
- **Design:** cost-consequence analysis (disaggregated costs and clinical consequences, as requested by the editor in comment 10), complemented by the cost per missed neoplastic progression avoided and its uncertainty. Quality-adjusted life years are not estimated because no validated utilities exist for this population. Reporting follows CHEERS 2022.
- **Data:** every value comes from the BANDING-SET database or from a cited source and is listed in the parameter registry with its location in the source.

---

# Overview of the methods

This section provides a stepwise description of the analyses performed.

## Objective and perspective

To compare the cost and the clinical consequences of three management strategies for a patient with an incidentally detected oesophageal or gastric SET of 10 mm or less. Perspective of the Spanish National Health System, with unit costs from the Catalan public health system (section 2.6); time horizon of 20 years in the base case. As the editor requested not to rely on long-term extrapolation of EBL-SINK efficacy (comment 4), 5- and 10-year horizons are also reported.

The 20-year horizon is a compromise between two requirements. It must be long enough to capture the consequences that differ between strategies: GIST progress slowly, and a neoplasm left behind after discharge may take years to become apparent. It should not, however, extend far beyond the evidence: the longest follow-up of small SETs under surveillance is about 10 years (median 80 months in Ho 2025; registry follow-up of 120 months in Kim 2022), and EBL-SINK has been followed for only 1 year. Twenty years therefore covers roughly twice the observed follow-up, while background mortality at the age of the cohort removes a growing share of patients from the model in the later years. Because a lifetime horizon lets residual disease after EBL-SINK accumulate for longer, it is examined as a check of the robustness of the dominance results (section 9.2).

## Population: closed cohort

The editor requested a **closed cohort** in which all strategies start from the same patients, and asked that the 0.36% detection yield per endoscopy not be used as an annual incidence (comments 1 and 2). Accordingly, the model follows a closed cohort of 1,000 patients whose lesion has already been detected, and results are reported per patient and per 1,000 patients. The three strategies start, by construction, with the same patients; test V2 in section 11 checks this. The characteristics of the cohort (age, sex, histology and layer of origin) come from BANDING-SET (section 6). As an exploratory secondary analysis that goes beyond the editor's requests, the budget impact is estimated separately with an **open cohort** (section 9.3), in which each year's new cases referred to the BANDING-SET network enter the model; this entry is a flow of referred cases, not a detection yield applied to the whole population.

## Strategies compared

The editor requested a comparator consistent with ESGE 2022, including selective EUS, and no surveillance after benign histology (comment 5). Three strategies are therefore compared:

- **Strategy A — EGD surveillance (ESGE):** oesophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) at 3–6 months and then every 2–3 years (ESGE 2022 recommendation 5). Base case: every 3 years, the least costly interval compatible with the guideline, so as not to overestimate the cost of the comparator.
- **Strategy B — Selective EUS surveillance (ESGE):** as strategy A, but lesions arising from the deep layer (muscularis propria) are followed with endoscopic ultrasound (EUS).
- **Strategy C — EUS plus EBL-SINK:** the stepwise alternative strategy of the study protocol: (i) baseline EUS with band ligation (without resection) and SINK biopsy for the whole cohort, with discharge if histology is benign (ESGE recommendation 4); (ii) conventional endoscopy (EGD) at 1 year for non-specific or potentially malignant histology, with discharge if the lesion has disappeared; (iii) surveillance alternating EUS and EGD every 2 years (starting with EUS at year 3) only for lesions that persist. Technical failures and patients who miss the 1-year control follow the same alternating surveillance.

## Model structure

The editor requested that histology, diagnosis, treatment and progression be modelled separately (comment 3), and that transitions be complete, sourced and internally consistent (comment 6).

We used a Markov model, a standard tool in health economics for following a group of patients over time. Its logic is simple:

- At any moment, each patient is in one of a small number of health states, for example "under surveillance, lesion stable" or "discharged".
- Time advances in steps of one year (cycles). In each cycle, a fixed proportion of the patients in each state moves to another state or stays where it is; these proportions are the transition probabilities.
- Each state and each move carries costs and clinical events (an endoscopy, a resection, an adverse event). Adding them up over 20 years gives the total costs and consequences of each strategy.
- Rather than simulating individual patients, the model tracks the proportion of a cohort of 1,000 patients in each state.

The model has six states (section 8.3). In the two-letter codes, the first letter is how the patient is managed (**S** = surveillance, **D** = discharged) and the second is the status of the lesion (**U** = unprogressed, **P** = progressed but not yet detected):

- **SU** (surveillance, unprogressed): under surveillance, no progression.
- **SP** (surveillance, progressed): under surveillance; the lesion has progressed, but this has not yet been detected.
- **DU** (discharged, unprogressed): discharged from follow-up, no progression.
- **DP** (discharged, progressed): discharged; the lesion has progressed unnoticed (missed neoplasm).
- **TR** (treated): the lesion has been resected or eradicated.
- **DEATH**: death from any cause.

Three features address the editor's comments:

1. **Histology is hidden but real.** From the start, each lesion is benign, GIST or NET, in the proportions observed in BANDING-SET, and the same states are run for each histology. A discharged benign lesion is therefore harmless, whereas a discharged GIST or NET can progress unnoticed.
2. **Progression and detection are separate.** Lesions progress at their biological rate whether or not anyone is looking. A progression is only detected at a scheduled visit, and only if the patient attends and the test picks it up.
3. **Treatment is not assumed to be perfect.** Resection may be incomplete, and a lesion that disappears after banding may leave residual disease.

Every year the same order of events applies: scheduled visit (if one is due), death from other causes, then biological progression. The strategies differ only in where patients start and how they are followed: in strategies A and B everyone starts in SU; in strategy C the initial EBL-SINK places each patient in SU, DU or TR according to its result. Cycles are annual and reported as such, which avoids the artefact of the previous model, which presented products of annual matrices as biennial probabilities (comment 6).

## Clinical parameters

- **BANDING-SET database:** population characteristics and EBL-SINK outcomes (technical success, diagnostic yield, disappearance at 1 year, adverse events, anaesthetist sedation and attendance at the 1-year control). They are estimated directly from the patient-level data when the database is available and stored in the parameter registry as events / total, so the report can be reproduced without the raw data (section 8.1).
- **Published literature:** natural history, surveillance, diagnosis, treatment, adverse events and costs, each with its page or table (section 8.2). The meta-analysis by Dong et al. (2025), recommended by the editor, provides the effect of deep-layer origin on progression, the relative detection of growth by EGD, the absence of GIST-related deaths and the overall progression rate of SETs <1 cm used as an external check (section 11). Every literature value was checked against the full text of its source and the registry records where in the source it was taken from.
- **Structural assumptions:** listed in section 7.

## Costs

The editor requested that costs be reconciled and complete, including the prior EUS, adverse events and repeat procedures (comment 7). Costs are expressed in 2025 euros from the perspective of the Spanish National Health System and are valued with unit costs from the Catalan public health system. Endoscopic procedures, hospital stay and pathology are valued with the standard direct cost from Loras et al. (2018), calculated by micro-costing in a Catalan hospital under the 2015 collective agreement, and are updated with the consumer price index (CPI) of the Spanish National Statistics Institute (INE; 2025 annual mean / 2015 annual mean). Loras 2018 includes the anaesthetist in endoscopic ultrasound and pathology in EUS-FNB and in resections, so these are not charged separately. Services not included in Loras 2018 (diagnostic EGD and management of adverse events after resection) are taken from the public tariffs of the Institut Català de la Salut in force in 2025 (Resolució SLT/4583/2024), which are not re-indexed. The EBL-SINK devices (ligation device, needle-knife and biopsy forceps), which Loras 2018 does not itemise, are valued at the 2018 market prices provided by the co-author of that study, updated to 2025 euros with the same CPI series (2025 annual mean / 2018 annual mean). Each procedure carries its own adverse event rate: EBL-SINK (BANDING-SET), endoscopic resection (Meng 2023), perforation during the diagnostic EGD or EUS at each visit (ASGE 2012) and EUS-FNB (Verloop 2024). **All** patients in strategy C bear the cost of the EBL-SINK procedure and its controls, which corrects defect B1 of the audit (test V11).

## Outcomes

Costs and effects are discounted at the same rate, 3% per year (parameter X01, following the Spanish guideline of Trapero-Bertran et al., 2025). Every measure that combines cost and effect (cost per missed progression avoided, cost-effectiveness plane, acceptability curve, net monetary benefit, value of information, dominance, one-way, scenario and threshold analyses) uses discounted effects, so that costs and effects are treated alike. As requested by the editor (comment 10) and in line with CHEERS 2022, the disaggregated table of costs and consequences reports discounted costs and **undiscounted** clinical events and resource use in natural units, together with the discounted number of missed progressions used as the effect measure. The number needed to treat is a clinical count and uses undiscounted events. The annual budget impact is undiscounted, as recommended by budget impact guidelines. The outcomes are:

- Total cost per patient.
- Procedures: EGD, EUS, EBL-SINK, EUS-guided sampling and endoscopic resections.
- Resections of benign lesions (unnecessary).
- Suspicious progression events.
- **Missed neoplastic progressions** (primary effectiveness outcome): progressions of a GIST or NET that are never detected within the horizon, whether they occur after discharge, remain undetected under surveillance at the end of the horizon or are still undetected when the patient dies from another cause. The same definition applies to every strategy.
- Discharges with residual disease: neoplasms discharged without having been eradicated.
- Adverse events (AEs) by procedure (EBL-SINK, resection, surveillance EGD/EUS and EUS-FNB).
- Person-years under surveillance (burden for the patient).
- Person-years lived with a progressed neoplasm that has not been detected (burden of missed disease), which captures not only whether a progression is missed but for how long.

## Uncertainty analysis

The editor requested that uncertainty be explored on the model inputs, with distributions taken from their sources, and with structural scenarios (comment 8). Uncertainty is therefore analysed on the **input parameters**, never on the model outputs:

- **One-way sensitivity analysis (OWSA):** each parameter with an interval in its source is set at its limits and **the model is re-run**.
- **Probabilistic sensitivity analysis (PSA):** `r format(params$n_psa, big.mark = ',')` iterations in the main analysis and `r format(params$n_dom, big.mark = ',')` per scenario in the secondary dominance analysis. Each iteration samples every uncertain parameter and re-runs the model for the three strategies with the same sampled values, which preserves the correlation between arms. Distributions: beta with a Jeffreys prior, Beta(x + 0.5, n − x + 0.5), for every proportion estimated from counts, whether from BANDING-SET or from published studies (so that proportions such as 29/29 retain uncertainty); beta fitted by the method of moments for published proportions reported only with a 95% CI or range (diagnostic yield of EUS-FNB and detection of growth by EGD relative to EUS); lognormal for rates and the odds ratio reported with a 95% CI (SD on the log scale = (ln upper − ln lower) / 3.92); gamma for rates whose plausible range starts at zero (progression of benign lesions and of NETs); and a Dirichlet distribution with the observed counts of benign, GIST and NET lesions for the histology mix.
- **Parameters kept fixed in the PSA:** age, surveillance schedules, unit costs and background mortality, which have no sampling uncertainty; the perforation and EUS-FNB adverse-event rates and the cost of managing a serious adverse event, which have a plausible range but no sampling distribution and are varied in the one-way analysis; the sensitivity of EUS for growth, varied in the threshold analysis; and the discount rate and surveillance interval, varied in the structural scenarios.
- **Structural scenarios:** those listed by the editor (comment 8): surveillance interval (examinations every 2 years in both surveillance strategies), time horizon (5 and 10 years), resection outcomes (ESGE reference values), endoscopic submucosal dissection for deep-layer lesions, published adverse-event rates of EBL-SINK, discount rate (0% and 5%), and lesions without a histological diagnosis assumed all benign or all neoplastic.
- **Threshold analysis:** on the parameters with the weakest evidence: residual disease after disappearance (H07, indirect evidence), detection of growth by EGD relative to EUS (V08) and detection of growth by EUS (V09, structural assumption).
- **Value of information:** the expected value of perfect information (EVPI) and of partial perfect information for groups of parameters (EVPPI) show which uncertainties would be worth resolving with further research (section 10.9).
- **Secondary dominance analysis:** attendance at surveillance by interval between examinations, to identify the conditions under which EUS plus EBL-SINK is less costly and leaves fewer undetected progressions (section 9.2).

## Verification and validation

The editor requested that the bootstrap not be presented as validation and that the sources of uncertainty be distinguished (comment 9). Five levels are therefore kept separate:

- First-order variability between patients (not applicable in a cohort model).
- Second-order parameter uncertainty (PSA).
- Monte Carlo error, with its standard error.
- Internal verification of the code (thirteen tests with synthetic values, section 11).
- Face validity against what was observed in BANDING-SET.

The bootstrap of the previous analysis is not reused as validation. Resampling the simulation outputs only measures Monte Carlo stability, which is reported here directly as the Monte Carlo standard error; it says nothing about whether the structure or the parameters of the model reflect reality.

```{r editor-matrix}
  "2", "Both strategies with the same cohort", "Common cohort by construction; automatic test V2", "11",
  "3", "Separate histology, diagnosis, treatment and progression; speak of a 'suspicious progression event'", "Latent histology B/GIST/NET; diagnosis with its own yield; treatment effect with residual disease; progression independent of detection; outcomes reported as suspicious progression events and missed neoplastic progressions", "2.4, 8.3, 8.4",
  "4", "Do not assume that disappearance eliminates the risk; model residual disease, discharges with residual disease and recurrence", "Residual disease after disappearance (H07) and discharges with residual disease; threshold analysis on residual disease; 5/10/20-year and lifetime horizons. Recurrence after complete resection is not modelled and is declared as an assumption", "7, 8.3, 9.2, 10.4, 10.5",
  "5", "Comparator consistent with ESGE; selective EUS; no surveillance if benign; pathways by location", "Both surveillance strategies follow ESGE 2022; discharge after benign histology; duodenum and rectum excluded from the base case by the guideline itself", "2.3, 4.1",
  "6", "Complete transitions, sources, time conversion, no inconsistencies", "Annual cycles without matrix products; same biology in all strategies; every transition with its source; GIST-specific mortality set to 0 as a declared assumption; endoscopic resection with <100% efficacy", "7, 8.2, 8.3, .Rmd file",
  "7", "Reconcile costs; prior EUS; complete costs; AEs and repeat procedures", "EBL-SINK (EUS, devices, pathology) charged to 100% of the cohort (test V11); 1-year control and later surveillance costed; repeat procedures; AEs of EBL-SINK, resection, diagnostic EGD/EUS and EUS-FNB", "2.6, 8.2, 11",
```

# Abbreviations

| Abbreviation | Meaning |
|---|---|
| AE | Adverse event |
| ASGE | American Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy |
| CEAC | Cost-effectiveness acceptability curve |
| CHEERS | Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards |
| CI | Confidence interval |
| CPI | Consumer price index |
| DRG | Diagnosis-related group |
| EBL | Endoscopic band ligation (without resection) |
| EGD | Oesophagogastroduodenoscopy |
| ESD | Endoscopic submucosal dissection |
| ESGE | European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy |
| EUS | Endoscopic ultrasound (endosonography) |
| EUS-FNA / EUS-FNB | EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration / biopsy |
| EVPI | Expected value of perfect information |
| EVPPI | Expected value of partial perfect information |
| GIST | Gastrointestinal stromal tumour |
| ICS | Institut Català de la Salut (Catalan Health Institute) |
| INE | Instituto Nacional de Estadística (Spanish National Statistics Institute) |
| IQR | Interquartile range |
| ISPOR | Professional Society for Health Economics and Outcomes Research |
| MAR / MNAR | Missing at random / missing not at random |
| NET | Neuroendocrine tumour |
| NMB | Net monetary benefit |
| NNT | Number needed to treat |
| OR | Odds ratio |
| OWSA | One-way sensitivity analysis |
| PSA | Probabilistic sensitivity analysis |
| QALY | Quality-adjusted life year |
| SD / SE | Standard deviation / standard error |
| SET / SEL | Subepithelial tumour / lesion |
| SINK | Single-incision needle-knife biopsy |
| WTP | Willingness to pay |

## Normality assessment {.tabset}

```{r normality-calc, eval=have_data}
norm_df <- tibble(Variable = c("Age (years)", "Size (mm)"),
                  x = list(an$edad, an$tam_mm)) |>
  mutate(n = map_int(x, ~ sum(!is.na(.x))),
         W = map_dbl(x, ~ sw_test(.x)$W),
         p = map_dbl(x, ~ sw_test(.x)$p),
         Decision = ifelse(p >= 0.05, "Compatible with normality", "Not normal: median (IQR)"))
```

```{r normality-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.8, eval=have_data}
p_qq <- ggplot(qq_df, aes(sample = v)) + stat_qq(colour = sjd_cols["purple_dk1"]) + stat_qq_line(colour = sjd_cols["red_dk1"]) +
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free") + labs(x = "Theoretical quantiles", y = "Observed quantiles") + theme_sjd()

skw <- function(x) { x <- x[!is.na(x)]; mean((x - mean(x))^3) / sd(x)^3 }
p_txt <- function(x) { v <- fmt_p(x); if (startsWith(v, "<")) paste0("p ", v) else paste0("p = ", v) }
age_d <- norm_df[norm_df$Variable == "Age (years)", ]; size_d <- norm_df[norm_df$Variable == "Size (mm)", ]

                   " (Shapiro-Wilk ", p_txt(age_d$p), "; ", if (age_d$p >= 0.05) "compatible with normality" else "not normally distributed", "). ",
                   "<b>Size:</b> values are concentrated at whole millimetres and at the 10 mm limit imposed by the selection, which appears as steps in the plot (Shapiro-Wilk ",
                   p_txt(size_d$p), "; ", if (size_d$p >= 0.05) "compatible with normality" else "not normally distributed", ")."))
```

# Key model assumptions

A model is only as credible as its assumptions. The table lists the simplifications of reality on which the model rests: choices for which there is no direct evidence and that could, in principle, be made differently. Values taken from the literature or from BANDING-SET are not assumptions, even when the evidence is indirect; their limitations are recorded in the parameter registry and their sources are listed in section 8.2. The management rules of each strategy are not assumptions either: they follow ESGE 2022 for strategies A and B and the study protocol for strategy C (section 2.3).

```{r assumptions-tbl}
assum <- tribble(
  ~`#`, ~Assumption, ~Justification, ~`How it is tested`,
  "1", "Annual cycles; within each cycle the order is scheduled visit, background death, biological progression.",
    "Surveillance intervals are whole years; with this order a lesion that progresses in a given year can only be detected at the next visit.", "2-year interval scenario (section 10.4).",
  "2", "Lesions without a histological diagnosis have the same distribution of benign, GIST and NET as those with a diagnosis (missing at random).",
    "No information is available on the histology of undiagnosed lesions.", "Scenarios with all unknown lesions benign or all neoplastic (section 10.4); Dirichlet sampling in the PSA.",
  "3", "The annual progression rate of each histology is constant over time and independent of age, time since detection and whether the lesion is being watched.",
    "The available cohorts report crude rates or rates per person-year, without evidence of change over time.", "One-way and probabilistic analyses on H04–H06; horizons of 5, 10 and 20 years and lifetime.",
  "4", "The odds ratio of progression for deep-layer origin (Dong 2025) is used as a rate ratio.",
    "Only estimate available; for rare events the odds ratio approximates the rate ratio.", "One-way and probabilistic analyses on H02; results by layer (section 9.1).",
  "5", "A progression is detected only at a scheduled visit; attendance is independent at each visit; symptomatic presentation between visits is not modelled.",
    "Small SETs are asymptomatic; attendance and detection are the mechanisms the editor asked to be modelled.", "One-way and probabilistic analyses on V07; dominance analysis by attendance and interval (section 9.2).",
  "6", "EUS detects every progression (V09 = 1).",
    "Progression is defined by EUS measurement in the source studies; no study has measured the sensitivity of EUS for growth.", "Threshold analysis on the detection of growth by EUS (section 10.7).",
  "7", "The ability of EGD to detect a progression, relative to EUS, equals the ratio of the growth rates observed under EGD-based and EUS-based surveillance in Dong 2025 (V08).",
    "No study has measured the sensitivity of EGD for the growth of a small SET; the ratio is the only available indirect measure.", "Threshold analysis on V08 (section 10.6).",
  "8", "After complete resection there are no further lesion-related events; a lesion that disappears after band ligation is eradicated except for a proportion H07 with residual disease, which is not followed after discharge.",
    "Recurrence after resection of small GIST is rare (2/199 in Meng 2023); residual disease after disappearance is the main uncertainty of EBL-SINK (editor comment 4).", "Threshold analysis on H07 (section 10.5); lifetime horizon (section 9.2).",
  "9", "There is no disease-specific mortality from small GIST or NET within the horizon (H08 = 0).",
    "No SET-related deaths in Kim 2022 (672 patients, 120 months) or Dong 2025; one GIST with liver metastasis in Ho 2025 (from a 6.2 mm lesion).", "Not varied; the primary outcome (missed progressions) captures the risk before death.",
  "10", "Every adverse event after resection, sampling or diagnostic endoscopy is costed as a serious event (C14), and adverse events carry no loss of quality of life.",
    "Conservative against the more procedure-intensive strategy; utilities are not available for this population.", "One-way analysis on T03, T04 and C14; published EBL-SINK adverse-event scenario."
)
sjd_kable(assum, caption = tab_n("Key structural assumptions of the model")) |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(2:4, width = "22em") |> cat_k()
```

# Primary analysis

```{r registry}
# ── Parameter registry ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
reg <- readxl::read_excel(reg_path, sheet = "Parametros")
reg <- reg |> mutate(across(c(valor, ic_bajo, ic_alto, eventos, total), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x))))

# ── Empirical BANDING-SET parameters ─────────────────────────────────────────
emp_row <- function(id, etiqueta, x, n) {
  ci <- wilson_ci(x, n)
  tibble(id = id, Parámetro = etiqueta, x = x, n = n, Estimación = x / n, IC_bajo = ci[1], IC_alto = ci[2])
}
if (have_data) {
# Re-estimated from the patient-level data every time the report is knitted
known   <- an |> filter(histo != "Unknown")
hc      <- table(factor(known$histo, levels = c("Benign", "GIST", "NET")))
tec_ok  <- an |> filter(tec_ok)
bx_eval <- tec_ok |> filter(!(bx_estado %in% c("Biòpsia prèvia: TNE")))
ctrl    <- need_ctrl |> mutate(eval1a = res_1a %in% c("1", "2", "NO ÈXIT A 4-6 SET"),
                               desap  = res_1a == "1")
ctrl_ev <- ctrl |> filter(eval1a)
emp <- bind_rows(
  emp_row("P02", "Women", sum(an$sexo == "Female", na.rm = TRUE), sum(!is.na(an$sexo))),
  emp_row("P03", "Benign histology (among known)", hc[["Benign"]], sum(hc)),
  emp_row("P04", "GIST (among known)", hc[["GIST"]], sum(hc)),
  emp_row("P05", "NET (among known)", hc[["NET"]], sum(hc)),
  emp_row("P06", "Deep layer", sum(an$capa == "Deep", na.rm = TRUE), sum(!is.na(an$capa))),
  emp_row("E01", "Technical success of EBL-SINK", sum(an$tec_ok), nrow(an)),
  emp_row("E02", "Diagnostic biopsy (SINK)", sum(bx_eval$bx_estado == "1"), nrow(bx_eval)),
  emp_row("E03", "Disappearance at 1 year — superficial layer", sum(ctrl_ev$desap & ctrl_ev$capa == "Superficial"), sum(ctrl_ev$capa == "Superficial")),
  emp_row("E04", "Disappearance at 1 year — deep layer", sum(ctrl_ev$desap & ctrl_ev$capa == "Deep"), sum(ctrl_ev$capa == "Deep")),
  emp_row("E05", "Adverse events of EUS plus EBL-SINK", sum(an$ea), nrow(an)),
  emp_row("E06", "Sedation by an anaesthetist", sum(an$sed_anest), nrow(an)),
  emp_row("E07", "1-year control assessed (if required)", nrow(ctrl_ev), nrow(ctrl))
)
edad0 <- median(an$edad, na.rm = TRUE)
n_an  <- nrow(an)

# Write into the registry: value, events and total for the DATA parameters
for (i in seq_len(nrow(emp))) {
  j <- which(reg$id == emp$id[i])
  reg$valor[j] <- emp$Estimación[i]; reg$eventos[j] <- emp$x[i]; reg$total[j] <- emp$n[i]
  reg$ic_bajo[j] <- emp$IC_bajo[i]; reg$ic_alto[j] <- emp$IC_alto[i]
}
reg$valor[reg$id == "P01"] <- edad0
} else {
# Taken from the registry (events and total stored from the last run with the data)
emp_ids <- c("P02", "P03", "P04", "P05", "P06", "E01", "E02", "E03", "E04", "E05", "E06", "E07")
emp <- map_dfr(emp_ids, function(id) {
  r <- reg[reg$id == id, ]
  if (is.na(r$eventos) || is.na(r$total)) stop("Registry row ", id, " has no events / total; the raw data are needed.")
  emp_row(id, r$parametro, r$eventos, r$total)
})
hc    <- setNames(emp$x[match(c("P03", "P04", "P05"), emp$id)], c("Benign", "GIST", "NET"))
edad0 <- reg$valor[reg$id == "P01"]
n_an  <- reg$total[reg$id == "P02"]
}

# ── Life table (sheet 'Mortalidad') ───────────────────────────────────────────
mort <- tryCatch(readxl::read_excel(reg_path, sheet = "Mortalidad"), error = function(e) NULL)
mort <- if (!is.null(mort)) mort |> mutate(across(everything(), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x)))) |> filter(!is.na(edad), !is.na(qx_hombres), !is.na(qx_mujeres)) else NULL
if (!is.null(mort) && nrow(mort) > 0) reg$valor[reg$id == "M01"] <- 1

# ── Completeness gate ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
opt_derive <- isTRUE(reg$valor[reg$id == "OPT01"] == 1)
req <- reg |> filter(requerido == "YES")
if (opt_derive) req <- req |> filter(!(id %in% c("H04", "H05", "H06")))
faltan    <- req |> filter(is.na(valor))
verificar <- reg |> filter(estado == "VERIFY")
listo <- nrow(faltan) == 0
```

## Model structure

```{r engine}
# =============================================================================
# EFI-BANDING-SET 2.0 — model engine (closed cohort, annual cycles)
# =============================================================================

# ---- Functions reused from EFI-BANDING-SET_0.2.R (lines 20-23 and 3205-3230)
clamp01  <- function(x) pmax(0, pmin(1, x))
p_from_h <- function(h, years = 1) 1 - exp(-h * years)
h_from_p <- function(p, years = 1) -log(1 - clamp01(p)) / years

fieller_ci <- function(delta_effect, delta_cost, alpha = 0.05) {
  n <- length(delta_effect); stopifnot(n == length(delta_cost), n > 2)
  muX <- mean(delta_effect, na.rm = TRUE); muY <- mean(delta_cost, na.rm = TRUE)
  varX <- var(delta_effect, na.rm = TRUE) / n
  varY <- var(delta_cost,   na.rm = TRUE) / n
  covXY <- cov(delta_effect, delta_cost, use = "complete.obs") / n
  z <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
  a <- muX^2 - z^2 * varX; b <- muX * muY - z^2 * covXY; c <- muY^2 - z^2 * varY
  disc <- b^2 - a * c; point <- muY / muX
  if (!is.finite(point)) point <- NA_real_
  if (a <= 0 || disc < 0) return(list(point = point, ci = c(NA_real_, NA_real_), type = "unbounded"))
  root <- sqrt(disc)
  list(point = point, ci = sort(c((b - root) / a, (b + root) / a)), type = "finite")
}

# ---- State space --------------------------------------------------------------
HIST   <- c("B", "G", "N")                    # benign, GIST, NET (latent histology)
MGMT   <- c("SU", "SP", "DU", "DP", "TR")     # surveillance without/with progression, discharged without/with progression, treated
STATES <- c(as.vector(outer(MGMT, HIST, paste, sep = "_")), "DEAD")
st <- function(m, h) paste(m, h, sep = "_")

# Cycles with a visit: visits at t = first + k*int, in cycle ceiling(t)
visit_cycles <- function(first, int, H) {
  if (first > H) return(integer(0))                 # horizon shorter than the first visit
  t <- seq(first, H, by = int)
  unique(pmin(H, pmax(1L, as.integer(ceiling(t - 1e-9)))))
}

# ---- One stratum (layer) of a strategy ------------------------------------------
run_stratum <- function(p, strategy = c("A", "B", "C"), layer = c("sup", "deep"), N = 1000) {
  strategy <- match.arg(strategy); layer <- match.arg(layer)
  H   <- p$horizon
  lam <- p$lambda[HIST] * if (layer == "deep") p$rr_deep else 1
  pr  <- p_from_h(lam, 1)                        # annual probability of progression by histology
  names(pr) <- HIST
  modality <- if (strategy == "B" && layer == "deep") "EUS" else "EGD"
  se   <- if (modality == "EUS") p$se_eus else p$se_egd
  cvis <- if (modality == "EUS") p$c_eus else p$c_egd
  c_er_L <- if (layer == "deep" && !is.null(p$c_er_deep)) p$c_er_deep else p$c_er
  int  <- if (modality == "EUS") p$int_eus else p$int_egd
  if (strategy == "C") {
    # EBL-SINK protocol (study protocol v1.0, step iii): lesions still under surveillance after the
    # 1-year EGD control are followed with EUS and EGD alternating every int_c years (EUS first)
    int_c <- if (is.null(p$int_c)) 2 else p$int_c
    vis <- visit_cycles(1 + int_c, int_c, H)
    mod_vis <- setNames(rep(c("EUS", "EGD"), length.out = length(vis)), vis)
  } else {
    vis <- visit_cycles(p$first_visit, int, H)
    mod_vis <- setNames(rep(modality, length(vis)), vis)
  }
  pdis <- if (layer == "deep") p$p_dis_deep else p$p_dis_sup
  df   <- function(t) 1 / (1 + p$disc)^(t - 0.5)       # mid-cycle discounting
  cpi  <- p$cpi

  m <- setNames(numeric(length(STATES)), STATES)
  ev <- c(n_egd = 0, n_eus = 0, n_ebl = 0, n_fnb = 0, n_er = 0, n_er_benign = 0,
          n_ae_ebl = 0, n_ae_er = 0, n_ae_endo = 0, n_ae_fnb = 0, prog_all = 0, prog_neo_missed = 0,
          neo_treated = 0, false_reassurance = 0, py_surv = 0, deaths = 0)
  ev_d  <- ev
  cost  <- 0; cost_d <- 0
  cost_t <- numeric(H + 1)                               # undiscounted cost per cycle (t = 0..H), for the budget impact
  ae_endo <- if (is.null(p$ae_endo)) 0 else p$ae_endo    # AEs per diagnostic EGD/EUS
  ae_fnb  <- if (is.null(p$ae_fnb))  0 else p$ae_fnb     # AEs per EUS-FNB
  add_ev <- function(name, x, t) { x <- unname(x); ev[name] <<- ev[name] + x; ev_d[name] <<- ev_d[name] + x * (if (t == 0) 1 else df(t)) }
  add_cost <- function(x, t) { x <- unname(x); cost <<- cost + x * cpi; cost_d <<- cost_d + x * cpi * (if (t == 0) 1 else df(t)); cost_t[t + 1] <<- cost_t[t + 1] + x * cpi }

  c_ebl_session <- p$c_eus + p$c_devices + p$c_path + p$c_sed_anest * p$p_sed_anest
  mass <- N * p$pi[HIST]; names(mass) <- HIST

  # ---- t = 0: initial situation
  if (strategy %in% c("A", "B")) {
    for (h in HIST) m[st("SU", h)] <- mass[h]
  } else {
    add_ev("n_ebl", N, 0); add_cost(N * c_ebl_session, 0)
    add_ev("n_ae_ebl", N * p$p_ae_ebl, 0); add_cost(N * p$p_ae_ebl * p$c_stay, 0)
    ctrl <- 0
    for (h in HIST) {
      tf  <- mass[h] * (1 - p$p_tech)
      ts  <- mass[h] * p$p_tech
      dx  <- ts * p$p_dx
      ndx <- ts * (1 - p$p_dx)
      m[st("SU", h)] <- m[st("SU", h)] + tf
      if (h == "B") {
        m[st("DU", "B")] <- m[st("DU", "B")] + dx               # discharge after benign histology (ESGE rec. 4)
        need <- ndx
      } else {
        need <- dx + ndx
      }
      att <- need * p$p_att1; noatt <- need * (1 - p$p_att1)
      ctrl <- ctrl + att
      m[st("SU", h)] <- m[st("SU", h)] + noatt                  # no 1-year control -> surveillance
      dis  <- att * pdis
      pers <- att * (1 - pdis)
      # disappearance: eradicated or residual (discharge with residual disease)
      m[st("TR", h)] <- m[st("TR", h)] + dis * (1 - p$p_res)
      m[st("DU", h)] <- m[st("DU", h)] + dis * p$p_res
      if (h != "B") add_ev("false_reassurance", dis * p$p_res, 1)
      # persisting lesion at the 1-year control (any histology) -> alternating EUS/EGD surveillance (protocol step iii)
      m[st("SU", h)] <- m[st("SU", h)] + pers
      if (h != "B") add_ev("neo_treated", dis * (1 - p$p_res), 1)
    }
    add_ev("n_egd", ctrl, 1); add_cost(ctrl * p$c_egd, 1)
    add_ev("n_ae_endo", ctrl * ae_endo, 1); add_cost(ctrl * ae_endo * p$c_ae_er, 1)
  }

  trace <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = H + 1, ncol = length(STATES), dimnames = list(0:H, STATES))
  trace[1, ] <- m

  # ---- Cycles 1..H
  for (t in seq_len(H)) {
    surv_start <- sum(m[st(c("SU", "SP"), HIST)])
    # (1) surveillance visit at the start of the cycle
    if (t %in% vis) {
      mod_t <- mod_vis[[as.character(t)]]
      se    <- if (mod_t == "EUS") p$se_eus else p$se_egd
      cvis  <- if (mod_t == "EUS") p$c_eus else p$c_egd
      attend <- p$c_att * surv_start
      add_ev(if (mod_t == "EUS") "n_eus" else "n_egd", attend, t); add_cost(attend * cvis, t)
      add_ev("n_ae_endo", attend * ae_endo, t); add_cost(attend * ae_endo * p$c_ae_er, t)
      for (h in HIST) {
        det <- m[st("SP", h)] * p$c_att * se
        if (det <= 0) next
        m[st("SP", h)] <- m[st("SP", h)] - det
        add_ev("n_fnb", det, t); add_cost(det * p$c_fnb, t)                  # EUS-FNB (Loras) already includes cytology/pathology
        add_ev("n_ae_fnb", det * ae_fnb, t); add_cost(det * ae_fnb * p$c_ae_er, t)
        if (h == "B") {
          dxb <- det * p$fnb_yield
          m[st("DU", "B")] <- m[st("DU", "B")] + dxb                # benign diagnosed -> discharge
          erb <- det - dxb                                           # non-diagnostic -> diagnostic resection (ESGE rec. 8)
          add_ev("n_er", erb, t); add_ev("n_er_benign", erb, t)
          add_cost(erb * c_er_L, t)
          add_ev("n_ae_er", erb * p$er_ae, t); add_cost(erb * p$er_ae * p$c_ae_er, t)
          m[st("TR", "B")] <- m[st("TR", "B")] + erb
        } else {
          add_ev("n_er", det, t); add_cost(det * c_er_L, t)
          add_ev("n_ae_er", det * p$er_ae, t); add_cost(det * p$er_ae * p$c_ae_er, t)
          m[st("TR", h)] <- m[st("TR", h)] + det * p$er_complete
          m[st("SU", h)] <- m[st("SU", h)] + det * (1 - p$er_complete)
          add_ev("neo_treated", det * p$er_complete, t)
        }
      }
    }
    m_start <- m
    # (2) background mortality
    q <- p$qx[t]
    alive <- setdiff(STATES, "DEAD")
    d <- m[alive] * q
    add_ev("deaths", sum(d), t)
    # a progressed GIST/NET still undetected under surveillance at death from another cause is never detected -> missed
    # (same definition as after discharge, where a progression counts as missed whatever happens later)
    add_ev("prog_neo_missed", sum(d[st("SP", c("G", "N"))]), t)
    m[alive] <- m[alive] - d; m["DEAD"] <- m["DEAD"] + sum(d)
    # (3) biological progression, independent of detection
    for (h in HIST) {
      a <- m[st("SU", h)] * pr[h]; m[st("SU", h)] <- m[st("SU", h)] - a; m[st("SP", h)] <- m[st("SP", h)] + a
      b <- m[st("DU", h)] * pr[h]; m[st("DU", h)] <- m[st("DU", h)] - b; m[st("DP", h)] <- m[st("DP", h)] + b
      add_ev("prog_all", a + b, t)
      if (h != "B") add_ev("prog_neo_missed", b, t)               # neoplastic progression after discharge
    }
    # (4) person-years under surveillance (trapezoid: half-cycle correction)
    surv_end <- sum(m[st(c("SU", "SP"), HIST)])
    add_ev("py_surv", (surv_start + surv_end) / 2, t)
    trace[t + 1, ] <- m
  }
  # progressed neoplasms still undetected (alive) at the end of the horizon
  add_ev("prog_neo_missed", sum(m[st("SP", c("G", "N"))]), H)
  list(events = ev, events_disc = ev_d, cost = cost, cost_disc = cost_d, cost_t = cost_t, trace = trace)
}

# ---- Full strategy: mixture of strata by layer --------------------------------
run_strategy <- function(p, strategy, N = 1000) {
  w <- c(sup = 1 - p$prop_deep, deep = p$prop_deep)
  out <- lapply(names(w), function(L) run_stratum(p, strategy, L, N))
  names(out) <- names(w)
  comb <- function(f) Reduce(`+`, Map(function(o, wt) f(o) * wt, out, w))
  list(events      = comb(function(o) o$events),
       events_disc = comb(function(o) o$events_disc),
       cost        = comb(function(o) o$cost),
       cost_disc   = comb(function(o) o$cost_disc),
       cost_t      = comb(function(o) o$cost_t),
       trace       = comb(function(o) o$trace),
       strata      = out)
}

run_all <- function(p, N = 1000) setNames(lapply(c("A", "B", "C"), function(s) run_strategy(p, s, N)), c("A", "B", "C"))

```

```{r engine-tests}
# =============================================================================
# Internal verification battery of the engine (editor comment 9)
# The 'fixture' values are SYNTHETIC: they only serve to check that the
# code does what it should. They are NOT study parameters and produce no results.
# =============================================================================
fixture <- function(H = 20) list(
  horizon = H, pi = c(B = 0.8, G = 0.15, N = 0.05),
  lambda = c(B = 0.01, G = 0.05, N = 0.02), rr_deep = 2, prop_deep = 0.3,
  qx = rep(0.01, H), disc = 0.03,
  p_tech = 0.95, p_dx = 0.65, p_dis_sup = 0.9, p_dis_deep = 0.8, p_att1 = 0.9,
  p_res = 0.1, p_ae_ebl = 0.05, p_sed_anest = 0.8,
  c_att = 0.8, se_egd = 0.6, se_eus = 0.9, first_visit = 0.5, int_egd = 3, int_eus = 3, int_c = 2,
  fnb_yield = 0.84, er_complete = 0.86, er_ae = 0.18,
  c_egd = 100, c_eus = 300, c_devices = 285, c_path = 50, c_sed_anest = 100,
  c_fnb = 1000, c_er = 1000, c_stay = 240, c_ae_er = 500, cpi = 1)

verify_engine <- function() {
  res <- list()
  chk <- function(id, desc, ok, detalle = "") res[[length(res) + 1]] <<- data.frame(
    Test = id, Description = desc, Result = if (isTRUE(ok)) "Pass" else "FAIL",
    Detail = detalle, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  N <- 1000
  # V1 population conservation in all cycles and strategies
  f <- fixture(); r <- run_all(f, N)
  dev <- max(sapply(r, function(x) max(abs(rowSums(x$trace) - N))))
  chk("V1", "Population conservation (sum of states = N in every cycle, 3 strategies)", dev < 1e-8,
      sprintf("maximum deviation = %.2e", dev))
  # V2 same starting cohort in all strategies
  n0 <- sapply(r, function(x) sum(x$trace[1, ]))
  chk("V2", "The three strategies start from the same cohort (N and histology)", all(abs(n0 - N) < 1e-9),
      paste(sprintf("%s=%.0f", names(n0), n0), collapse = "; "))
  # V3 no biological progression -> zero progression events
  f3 <- fixture(); f3$lambda[] <- 0
  r3 <- run_all(f3, N); pe <- sapply(r3, function(x) x$events["prog_all"])
  chk("V3", "Progression rate = 0 produces 0 progression events", all(pe == 0), paste(round(pe, 6), collapse = "; "))
  # V4 mortality = 1 -> everyone dead at the end of cycle 1
  f4 <- fixture(); f4$qx[] <- 1
  r4 <- run_all(f4, N); dead1 <- sapply(r4, function(x) x$trace["1", "DEAD"])
  chk("V4", "Mortality = 1 leaves the whole cohort in DEATH after cycle 1", all(abs(dead1 - N) < 1e-8),
      paste(round(dead1, 6), collapse = "; "))
  # V5 identical strategy -> zero increment
  rA1 <- run_strategy(f, "A", N); rA2 <- run_strategy(f, "A", N)
  chk("V5", "A strategy compared with itself gives an increment in cost and effects = 0",
      rA1$cost_disc - rA2$cost_disc == 0 && all(rA1$events - rA2$events == 0))
  # V6 no residual disease -> no discharge with residual disease
  f6 <- fixture(); f6$p_res <- 0
  r6 <- run_strategy(f6, "C", N)
  chk("V6", "Residual disease = 0 implies discharges with residual disease = 0 and no neoplastic progression after discharge",
      r6$events["false_reassurance"] == 0 && all(r6$trace[, c("DP_G", "DP_N")] < 1e-9))
  # V7 monotonicity: more residual disease -> more undetected neoplasms
  fr <- sapply(c(0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4), function(x) { g <- fixture(); g$p_res <- x; run_strategy(g, "C", N)$events["prog_neo_missed"] })
  chk("V7", "More residual disease produces more missed neoplastic progressions (monotonic)",
      all(diff(fr) > 0), paste(round(fr, 3), collapse = " < "))
  # V8 discount 0 -> discounted = undiscounted
  f8 <- fixture(); f8$disc <- 0; r8 <- run_all(f8, N)
  d8 <- max(sapply(r8, function(x) abs(x$cost - x$cost_disc)))
  chk("V8", "With a discount rate of 0, discounted cost = undiscounted cost", d8 < 1e-6, sprintf("max. diff. = %.2e", d8))
  # V9 face validity: the model reproduces the EBL-SINK entry cascade
  g <- fixture(); g$lambda[] <- 0; g$qx[] <- 0; g$p_res <- 0
  s <- run_stratum(g, "C", "sup", N)
  exp_B_dis <- N * g$pi["B"] * g$p_tech * g$p_dx
  chk("V9", "Face validity: discharges for benign histology = N·π_B·technical success·diagnostic yield",
      abs(s$trace[1, "DU_B"] - exp_B_dis) < 1e-8, sprintf("model = %.3f; expected = %.3f", s$trace[1, "DU_B"], exp_B_dis))
  # V10 extreme values: no effective surveillance (attendance 0) -> no visits or detections in A
  f10 <- fixture(); f10$c_att <- 0; r10 <- run_strategy(f10, "A", N)
  chk("V10", "Attendance 0 at surveillance removes visits and resections in strategy A",
      r10$events["n_egd"] == 0 && r10$events["n_er"] == 0)
  # V11 EBL-SINK is charged to the WHOLE cohort (audit defect B1)
  rC <- run_strategy(f, "C", N)
  chk("V11", "The EBL-SINK procedure is charged to 100% of the cohort (corrects audit defect B1)",
      abs(rC$events["n_ebl"] - N) < 1e-9, sprintf("procedures = %.1f of %d", rC$events["n_ebl"], N))
  # V12 the cost per cycle (budget impact) adds up to the total undiscounted cost
  f12 <- fixture(); f12$ae_endo <- 0.001; f12$ae_fnb <- 0.02; r12 <- run_all(f12, N)
  d12 <- max(sapply(r12, function(x) abs(sum(x$cost_t) - x$cost)))
  chk("V12", "The sum of the cost per cycle equals the total undiscounted cost (basis of the budget impact)", d12 < 1e-6, sprintf("max. diff. = %.2e", d12))
  # V13 no detection and no benign lesions -> every progression is missed, whether the patient is alive or dead at the end
  f13 <- fixture(); f13$c_att <- 0; f13$pi <- c(B = 0, G = 0.75, N = 0.25); r13 <- run_strategy(f13, "A", N)
  chk("V13", "Without detection, every neoplastic progression counts as missed, including those of patients who die before the end of the horizon",
      abs(r13$events["prog_neo_missed"] - r13$events["prog_all"]) < 1e-8,
      sprintf("missed = %.3f; progressions = %.3f", r13$events["prog_neo_missed"], r13$events["prog_all"]))
  do.call(rbind, res)
}
```

```{r model-build}
# ── From registry to engine parameter list ────────────────────────────────────
HORIZON <- 20
cohort_qx <- function(age0, fem, H) {
  if (is.null(mort) || nrow(mort) == 0) return(rep(NA_real_, H))
  a <- pmin(round(age0) + seq_len(H) - 1, max(mort$edad))
  qh <- mort$qx_hombres[match(a, mort$edad)]; qm <- mort$qx_mujeres[match(a, mort$edad)]
  (1 - fem) * qh + fem * qm
}
cost_2015_ids <- reg$id[grepl("2015", reg$bloque)]   # Loras 2018 (2015 €): updated with the CPI (C16)
cost_2018_ids <- reg$id[grepl("market price", reg$bloque)]   # device market prices (2018 €): updated with the CPI (C18)
build_p <- function(v, H = HORIZON) {
  u <- function(id) unname(v[id])
  uc <- function(id) u(id) * (if (id %in% cost_2015_ids) u("C16") else if (id %in% cost_2018_ids) u("C18") else 1)   # cost in 2025 euros
  lam <- if (opt_derive) {
    piG <- u("P04"); c(B = u("H01") * (1 - u("H03")) / (1 - piG), G = u("H01") * u("H03") / piG, N = u("H01") * (1 - u("H03")) / (1 - piG))
  } else c(B = u("H04"), G = u("H05"), N = u("H06"))
  pis <- c(B = u("P03"), G = u("P04"), N = u("P05")); pis <- pis / sum(pis)
  list(horizon = H, pi = pis, lambda = lam, rr_deep = u("H02"), prop_deep = u("P06"),
       qx = cohort_qx(u("P01"), u("P02"), H), disc = u("X01"),
       p_tech = u("E01"), p_dx = u("E02"), p_dis_sup = u("E03"), p_dis_deep = u("E04"), p_att1 = u("E07"),
       p_res = u("H07"), p_ae_ebl = u("E05"), p_sed_anest = u("E06"),
       c_att = u("V07"), se_egd = u("V08") * u("V09"), se_eus = u("V09"),   # V08 is relative to EUS
       first_visit = u("V01"), int_egd = u("V02"), int_eus = u("V03"), int_c = u("V10"),
       fnb_yield = u("D01"), er_complete = u("T01"), er_ae = u("T02"),
       c_egd = uc("C09"), c_eus = uc("C01"), c_devices = uc("C10") + uc("C11") + uc("C12"), c_path = uc("C08"),
       c_sed_anest = uc("C13"), c_fnb = uc("C02"), c_er = uc("C03"), c_stay = uc("C07"), c_ae_er = uc("C14"),
       ae_endo = u("T03"), ae_fnb = u("T04"),
       cpi = 1)                                             # price updating is already applied in uc()
}
v_base <- setNames(reg$valor, reg$id)

# ── Probabilistic sampling from the registry ──────────────────────────────────
beta_mom <- function(n, m, se) {
  if (is.na(se) || se <= 0) return(rep(m, n))
  k <- m * (1 - m) / se^2 - 1
  if (k <= 0) return(rep(m, n))
  rbeta(n, m * k, (1 - m) * k)
}
draw_row <- function(r, n) {
  if (is.na(r$valor)) return(rep(NA_real_, n))
  if (grepl("^fixed", r$distribucion %||% "")) return(rep(r$valor, n))  # range only for OWSA
  if (r$id %in% c("P03", "P04", "P05")) return(rep(r$valor, n))          # sampled jointly (Dirichlet)
  if (!is.na(r$eventos) && !is.na(r$total) && r$total > 0)
    return(rbeta(n, r$eventos + 0.5, r$total - r$eventos + 0.5))        # beta with Jeffreys prior
  if (!is.na(r$ic_bajo) && !is.na(r$ic_alto) && r$ic_alto > r$ic_bajo) {
    if (grepl("^gamma", r$distribucion %||% "") && r$valor > 0) {           # rates whose range starts at 0
      sdv <- (r$ic_alto - r$ic_bajo) / 3.92
      return(rgamma(n, shape = (r$valor / sdv)^2, rate = r$valor / sdv^2))
    }
    if (r$unidad == "proportion") return(beta_mom(n, r$valor, (r$ic_alto - r$ic_bajo) / 3.92))
    if (grepl("rate|OR", r$unidad) && r$ic_bajo > 0)
      return(rlnorm(n, log(r$valor), (log(r$ic_alto) - log(r$ic_bajo)) / 3.92))
  }
  rep(r$valor, n)
}
draw_psa <- function(n) {
  M <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(reg)), function(i) draw_row(reg[i, ], n)); colnames(M) <- reg$id
  g <- sapply(c("Benign", "GIST", "NET"), function(h) rgamma(n, shape = hc[[h]], rate = 1))
  g <- g / rowSums(g); M[, "P03"] <- g[, 1]; M[, "P04"] <- g[, 2]; M[, "P05"] <- g[, 3]
  M
}
```

```{r markov-calc}
if (listo) {
  p_base <- build_p(v_base)
  # One-year transition probabilities, base case, in a surveillance (visit) year.
  # Order of events within each cycle, as in the model engine: (1) visit and detection,
  # (2) background death, (3) biological progression.
  tp_stratum <- function(h, layer = "sup", modality = "EGD") {
    rr <- if (layer == "deep") p_base$rr_deep else 1
    pr <- p_from_h(p_base$lambda[[h]] * rr, 1)
    q  <- p_base$qx[1]
    se <- if (modality == "EUS") p_base$se_eus else p_base$se_egd
    d  <- p_base$c_att * se                                   # progression detected at the visit
    if (h == "B") { to_tr <- d * (1 - p_base$fnb_yield); to_back <- d * p_base$fnb_yield; back <- "DU"; back_prog <- "DP" }
    else          { to_tr <- d * p_base$er_complete;     to_back <- d * (1 - p_base$er_complete); back <- "SU"; back_prog <- "SP" }
    # Patients returned by the visit (benign sample -> discharged; incomplete resection -> surveillance)
    # can still progress later in the same cycle
    tibble(from = c("SU", "SU", "SU", "SP", "SP", "SP", "SP", "SP", "DU", "DU", "DU", "DP", "DP", "TR", "TR", "D"),
           to   = c("SU", "SP", "D", "SP", "TR", back, back_prog, "D", "DU", "DP", "D", "DP", "D", "TR", "D", "D"),
           p    = c((1 - q) * (1 - pr), (1 - q) * pr, q,
                    (1 - d) * (1 - q), to_tr * (1 - q), to_back * (1 - q) * (1 - pr), to_back * (1 - q) * pr, q,
                    (1 - q) * (1 - pr), (1 - q) * pr, q, 1 - q, q, 1 - q, q, 1)) |>
      group_by(from, to) |> summarise(p = sum(p), .groups = "drop")
  }
  tp_g <- tp_stratum("G", "sup", "EGD") |> mutate(from = ifelse(from == "D", "DEATH", from), to = ifelse(to == "D", "DEATH", to))
  stopifnot(all(abs(tapply(tp_g$p, tp_g$from, sum) - 1) < 1e-12))   # each row sums to 1
  # Initial state distribution of the GIST, deep-layer stratum in each strategy (from the engine)
  init <- map_dfr(c("A", "B", "C"), function(sname) {
    tr0 <- run_stratum(p_base, sname, "deep", 1)$trace[1, ]
    g <- tr0[paste0(c("SU", "SP", "DU", "DP", "TR"), "_G")] / p_base$pi[["G"]]
    tibble(Strategy = S_LAB[[sname]], SU = g[[1]], DU = g[[3]], TR = g[[5]])
  })
}
```

```{r markov-dots}
if (listo) {
  # One diagram per strategy, same example stratum (GIST arising from the deep layer) in a year with a scheduled visit.
  # Drawn with ggplot2 at fixed positions with hand-set curves, so that no arrow is rerouted automatically.
  fmt_p <- function(x) ifelse(x < 0.01, formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 4), formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3))
  # Markov diagram drawn with ggplot2: fixed positions and hand-set curves (no automatic routing)
  markov_gg <- function(tp, i0, fmt_p, labels = TRUE) {        # labels = FALSE: states and arrows only (manuscript Figure 1)
    r <- 0.42
    P <- tibble::tribble(~node, ~x, ~y, ~fill,
      "SU", 2.4, 1.5, "#D6EAF8", "SP", 4.3, 1.25, "#FCE4D6", "TR", 6.4, 0, "#D5F5E3",
      "DEATH", 8.4, 0, "#E8E8E8", "DU", 2.4, -1.5, "#D6EAF8", "DP", 4.3, -1.5, "#FCE4D6")
    xy <- function(n) unlist(P[P$node == n, c("x", "y")])
    on_circle <- function(n, deg) xy(n) + r * c(cos(deg * pi / 180), sin(deg * pi / 180))
    # edge geometry: departure / arrival angle on each circle and curvature (negative = bulges to the left)
    geo <- tibble::tribble(~from, ~to, ~a1, ~a2, ~curv,
      "SU", "SP", -15, 195, 0.18,  "SP", "SU", 165, 15, 0.18,
      "SU", "SP", NA, NA, NA,
      "SP", "TR", -45, 135, 0,     "TR", "DEATH", 0, 180, 0,
      "DU", "DP", 0, 180, 0,       "DP", "DEATH", 15, 215, -0.08,
      "SU", "DEATH", 50, 105, -0.55, "SP", "DEATH", 20, 135, -0.45, "DU", "DEATH", -50, 255, 0.5,
      "SP", "DU", 235, 55, 0,      "SP", "DP", 258, 140, 0,      # benign lesions only: detected, sampled and discharged
      "TR", "SU", NA, NA, NA) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(a1))
    e <- dplyr::inner_join(tp, geo, by = c("from", "to"))
    seg <- purrr::pmap_dfr(e, function(from, to, p, a1, a2, curv, ...) {
      s <- on_circle(from, a1); t <- on_circle(to, a2); m <- (s + t) / 2; d <- t - s; L <- sqrt(sum(d^2))
      nrm <- c(d[2], -d[1]) / L                                   # unit normal to the right of the direction of travel
      lab <- m + nrm * curv * L / 2 + (if (curv == 0) c(-d[2], d[1]) / L * 0.14 else nrm * sign(curv) * 0.13)
      tibble::tibble(from, to, p, curv, x = s[1], y = s[2], xend = t[1], yend = t[2], lx = lab[1], ly = lab[2])
    })
    seg$col <- ifelse(seg$from == "SP" & seg$to %in% c("TR", "SU", "DU", "DP"), "#D62839", "#7F7F7F")
    # self-loops on top of each circle
    loops <- dplyr::filter(tp, from == to) |> dplyr::inner_join(P, by = c("from" = "node"))
    loop_path <- purrr::pmap_dfr(loops, function(from, p, x, y, ...) {
      if (from == "DEATH") {                                       # DEATH: loop on the right-hand side
        th <- seq(125, -125, length.out = 60) * pi / 180; cx <- x + r + 0.16; cy <- y
        return(tibble::tibble(from, p, px = cx + 0.2 * cos(th), py = cy + 0.2 * sin(th), lx = cx + 0.42, ly = cy))
      }
      th <- seq(215, -35, length.out = 60) * pi / 180; cx <- x; cy <- y + r + 0.16
      tibble::tibble(from, p, px = cx + 0.2 * cos(th), py = cy + 0.2 * sin(th), lx = cx, ly = cy + 0.32)
    })
    loop_path$col <- ifelse(loop_path$from == "SP", "#D62839", "#7F7F7F")
    # entry arrows from the detection box
    box <- c(x = 0, y = 0, w = 1.5, h = 0.62)
    ent <- tibble::tibble(to = names(i0), p = as.numeric(i0))
    ent_geo <- tibble::tribble(~to, ~sx, ~sy, ~a2, ~curv, "SU", 0.55, 0.31, 215, 0, "TR", 0.75, 0, 180, 0, "DU", 0.55, -0.31, 145, 0)
    ent <- dplyr::inner_join(ent, ent_geo, by = "to") |>
      dplyr::mutate(xend = purrr::map2_dbl(to, a2, ~ on_circle(.x, .y)[1]), yend = purrr::map2_dbl(to, a2, ~ on_circle(.x, .y)[2]),
                    lx = (sx + xend) / 2 + ifelse(to == "TR", 0, ifelse(to == "SU", -0.12, -0.12)), ly = (sy + yend) / 2 + ifelse(to == "TR", 0.12, ifelse(to == "SU", 0.1, -0.1)))
    circ <- purrr::pmap_dfr(P, function(node, x, y, fill) { th <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 120); tibble::tibble(node, fill, cx = x + r * cos(th), cy = y + r * sin(th)) })
    arw <- grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(2.2, "mm"), type = "closed")
    g <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
      ggplot2::annotate("rect", xmin = box["x"] - box["w"] / 2, xmax = box["x"] + box["w"] / 2, ymin = box["y"] - box["h"] / 2, ymax = box["y"] + box["h"] / 2,
                        fill = "white", colour = "#4A5A8A", linewidth = 0.5) +
      ggplot2::annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = "SET ≤10 mm\ndetected", size = 3.6, lineheight = 0.95) +
      ggplot2::geom_segment(data = ent, ggplot2::aes(x = sx, y = sy, xend = xend, yend = yend), linetype = "dashed", colour = "#4A5A8A", linewidth = 0.45, arrow = arw) +
      (if (labels) ggplot2::geom_text(data = ent, ggplot2::aes(lx, ly, label = fmt_p(p)), colour = "#4A5A8A", size = 3.1))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(seg))) {
      sg <- seg[i, ]
      g <- g + ggplot2::geom_curve(data = sg, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend), curvature = sg$curv, ncp = 15,
                                   colour = sg$col, linewidth = if (sg$col == "#D62839") 0.9 else 0.45, arrow = arw)
    }
    g + (if (labels) ggplot2::geom_text(data = seg, ggplot2::aes(lx, ly, label = fmt_p(p), colour = I(col)), size = 3.1)) +
      ggplot2::geom_path(data = loop_path, ggplot2::aes(px, py, group = from, colour = I(col)), linewidth = 0.5, arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(1.8, "mm"), type = "closed")) +
      (if (labels) ggplot2::geom_text(data = dplyr::distinct(loop_path, from, p, lx, ly, col), ggplot2::aes(lx, ly, label = fmt_p(p), colour = I(col)), size = 3.1)) +
      ggplot2::geom_polygon(data = circ, ggplot2::aes(cx, cy, group = node, fill = I(fill)), colour = "#4A5A8A", linewidth = 0.6) +
      ggplot2::geom_text(data = P, ggplot2::aes(x, y, label = node), fontface = "bold", size = ifelse(P$node == "DEATH", 3.6, 4.4)) +
      ggplot2::coord_equal(xlim = c(-0.8, 9.6), ylim = c(-2.8, 3.25), expand = FALSE) + ggplot2::theme_void() + ggplot2::theme(plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA))
  }
  markov_plot_for <- function(sname, modality, labels = TRUE) {
    tp <- tp_stratum("G", "deep", modality) |> mutate(from = ifelse(from == "D", "DEATH", from), to = ifelse(to == "D", "DEATH", to))
    stopifnot(all(abs(tapply(tp$p, tp$from, sum) - 1) < 1e-12))
    # Structure-only version: every transition that exists in any stratum (adds SP -> DU/DP of benign lesions)
    if (!labels) tp <- dplyr::bind_rows(tp, tp_stratum("B", "deep", modality) |> mutate(from = ifelse(from == "D", "DEATH", from), to = ifelse(to == "D", "DEATH", to))) |>
      dplyr::distinct(from, to, .keep_all = TRUE)
    i0 <- unlist(init[init$Strategy == S_LAB[[sname]], c("SU", "DU", "TR")]); i0 <- i0[i0 > 1e-9]
    markov_gg(tp, i0, fmt_p, labels)
  }
  markov_plots <- list(A = markov_plot_for("A", "EGD"), B = markov_plot_for("B", "EUS"), C = markov_plot_for("C", "EUS"))
  for (k in names(markov_plots)) save_fig(markov_plots[[k]], paste0("fig_markov_model_", k), 10, 6.2)
  # Manuscript version (Figure 1B-D): states and arrows only; the probabilities are reported in the supplementary tables
  markov_plots_pub <- list(A = markov_plot_for("A", "EGD", FALSE), B = markov_plot_for("B", "EUS", FALSE), C = markov_plot_for("C", "EUS", FALSE))
  markov_common <- paste0(
    "Example: GIST arising from the deep layer (muscularis propria), in a year with a scheduled visit. ",
    "The box is the common starting point: an incidental SET of 10 mm or less has been detected; dashed arrows give the starting state in this strategy. ",
    "Grey arrows (progression and background death) are the same in the three strategies; red arrows (detection at the visit) depend on the strategy, the test and whether a visit is due that year, and are 0 in years without a visit. ",
    "SU = surveillance, unprogressed; SP = surveillance, progressed (not yet detected); DU = discharged, unprogressed; DP = discharged, progressed (missed neoplasm); TR = treated (resected or eradicated); DEATH = death from any cause. ",
    "Each circle's outgoing probabilities sum to 1; background death is shown for the first cycle (age ", round(v_base[["P01"]]), ")")
}
```
